Definition: a superlative probably from G2192 (in the sense of contiguity); farthest, final (of place or time):--ends of, last, latter end, lowest, uttermost.
BiblicalUsage: Éschatos means last — the farthest, the final, the end of the line. The last shall be first, Jesus says; the last enemy to be destroyed is death; and these are the last days, John says. It is the word for the end of things, and for what comes after the end.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe éschatos keeps me honest about the end: death is the last enemy, and it has already been defeated. I hold that living in the last days means living as if the end were near — because it is.
RelatedEvents: The Resurrection; The Rich Young Ruler
